Binned heatmap of events on a rink

Source: R/geom_rink_bin.R
geom_rink_bin.Rd

Bins events into a square grid and draws one square per cell, coloured by the mean of the z aesthetic (e.g. expected goals, or any per-event value). Squares are drawn in rink units and never exceed binwidth, so they tile the grid without overlapping and look identical at any export size. Add it to a rink from annotate_rink(); facet it however you like.

Usage

geom_rink_bin(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  style = c("size", "fill", "alpha"),
  binwidth = 2.5,
  gap = 0,
  alpha = NULL,
  dimensions = IIHF,
  xlim = NULL,
  ylim = NULL,
  precomputed = FALSE,
  scales = TRUE,
  diverging = FALSE,
  colour = NA,
  linewidth = 0,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

Arguments

mapping

Aesthetic mapping, usually aes(x, y, z) (often set on the ggplot() call), where z is averaged within each cell. fill, size and alpha are supplied by style; anything you map here overrides them. With precomputed = TRUE, the data needs value and n columns (as returned by rink_bin()).

data, position, na.rm, show.legend, inherit.aes

Standard ggplot2 layer arguments.

...

Other arguments passed to ggplot2::layer().

style

One of "size", "fill" or "alpha" (see Details).

binwidth

Cell size, in rink units. Also the largest square side.

gap

For "fill" and "alpha", the gap between squares in rink units (the square side is binwidth - gap).

alpha

Constant square alpha for "size" and "fill" (default 0.9). Ignored for "alpha", where alpha is mapped.

dimensions

Rink dimensions (e.g. IIHF, NHL) that set the binning bounds, so events on or behind the boards snap into the last in-rink cell. Pass the rink you are drawing, or NULL to bin without bounds. Ignored for any of xlim / ylim given, and when precomputed = TRUE.

xlim, ylim

Optional binning bounds in rink coordinates.

precomputed

If TRUE, skip binning and draw the cells as supplied, e.g. values you derived yourself from rink_bin().

scales

If TRUE (default), also return the matching scales for style: scale_fill_rink() (or scale_fill_rink_diverging() with diverging = TRUE) plus scale_size_rink() for "size" or scale_alpha_rink() for "alpha". Set FALSE to add your own.

diverging

Use the diverging fill scale, for maps of differences centred on 0 (e.g. a player minus league average).

colour, linewidth

Square border colour and width. The default draws no border; use e.g. colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3 for gridlines.

Value

A ggplot2 layer, or a list of a layer and scales.

Details

Three ready-made styles cover the common maps; pick one with style:

"size"

Square size encodes the event count (area proportional to frequency), fill the mean value.

"fill"

Constant-size squares that fill the cell (leave a gap for thin gridlines); fill encodes the mean value.

"alpha"

Constant-size squares whose alpha encodes the event count and fill the mean value.

Without a z aesthetic there is no value to average; map fill to after_stat(count) for a pure frequency map (see examples).

See also

rink_bin(), scale_fill_rink(), annotate_rink()

Examples

library(ggplot2)

base <- ggplot(shots, aes(x, y, z = xg)) +
  annotate_rink(orientation = "vertical", zones = "oz",
                colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.5)

base + geom_rink_bin(style = "size", binwidth = 2)

base + geom_rink_bin(style = "fill", binwidth = 2, gap = 0.1)

base + geom_rink_bin(style = "alpha", binwidth = 2)


# Frequency only: fill by count, your own scale
base +
  geom_rink_bin(aes(fill = after_stat(count)), style = "fill",
                binwidth = 2, scales = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_rink(name = "Shots", labels = NULL)
